newsitem.title: VIETNAM: IMF discusses soft-loans programme with Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: IMF discusses soft-loans programme with Vietnam.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund said on Friday it had discussed with Vietnam an economic programme needed for Hanoi to receive its third annual batch of Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility soft loans.
A statement said consensus had been reached during talks this week on the importance of further trade liberalisation, as well as reforms to the financial, tax and state-enterprise sectors.
It gave an upbeat assessment of Vietnam's economy and said it had remained on track so far this year with high growth and low inflation supported by strong macroeconomic policies.

Although the external current account deficit remained high, export growth was strong, and international reserves were increasing, it said. Hanoi had affirmed its commitment to the structural reform process, it said.

The IMF approved a three-year, six-tranche Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility (ESAF) of about $530 million for Vietnam in November 1994, following the success of reforms introduced by Hanoi in the late 1980s.

However, discussions on steps needed for the third and final year of the ESAF programme have been delayed. The IMF statement said further talks would be held later this year following a government reshuffle due in September.
ESAF's are funds lent by the IMF at low rates to low-income countries in return for a pledge to undertake strong policy steps, usually aimed at redressing balance of payment problems.
